name: Es Cavallet
village: Ses Salines natural park, Sant Josep
open: La Escollera — open all year, daily 13:00–19:00, log fire inside on grey days
walk: Es Cavallet → Torre de ses Portes watchtower, 40 min along the dunes
blurb: The long wild strand on the far side of the salt pans: dunes, a nudist stretch, and the first beach everyone goes to when the tramuntana blows, because the dunes and the headland take the wind. Water is calm and clear right through November.
tip: Park at the far (south) end for Escollera; the north end is for the walk.

name: Ses Salines
village: Ses Salines natural park, Sant Josep
open: NoHo Beach Club — Wed–Sun. Sa Trinxa closed for the winter. Jockey Club, Malibú: to confirm
walk: Salines → Sa Canal salt pans → Torre de ses Portes, 1 h
blurb: Fine white sand, pines right down to the beach, and the salt flats behind it with the flamingos from October on. In summer it's a scene; in winter it's a walk, a swim if you're brave, and a lunch if anything is open.
tip: The flamingos are at the salt pans by the Sa Canal road, best at low sun.

name: Es Torrent
walk: Es Torrent → Porroig → Cala Jondal coast path, 1 h 15
blurb: A pebble cove below Porroig with one of the island's great fish restaurants on it. Deep in the fold of the coast, so it's warm and still when the rest of the island is grey.
tip: Pebbles, not sand — bring something to sit on.

name: Cala d'Hort
open: To confirm — Es Boldadó, El Carmen
walk: Cala d'Hort → Sa Pedrera (Atlantis) viewpoint is closed; take the coast path south instead
blurb: The beach in front of Es Vedrà. In winter the rock goes orange at four in the afternoon and the restaurants on the slope are the best seats on the island for it — when they're open.
tip: Parking is restricted since 2025; arrive early or come by bike from Es Cubells.

name: Cala Comte
walk: Cala Comte → Cala Bassa → Cala Tarida coast path, 1 h 30 one way
blurb: Turquoise water, the islets of Es Bosc and Sa Conillera, and the island's most-watched sunset. Empty in winter apart from the dog walkers.
tip: The southern cove (Platja des Racó) is the sheltered one.

name: Cala Gració & Gracioneta
open: Hostal La Torre (Cap Negret, 10 min walk) — reopens 17 Nov, tapas from 13:00, the sunset bar. Gracioneta chiringuito: to confirm
walk: Cala Gració → Cap Negret → Cala Salada coast path, 1 h
blurb: Two small coves a ten-minute walk from Sant Antoni, facing west: calm water, a tiny beach shack, and a sunset you can walk home from.
tip: Gracioneta is the smaller, prettier one, reached by the path on the left.

name: Cala Salada & Saladeta
walk: Cala Salada → Ses Fontanelles cave paintings → Cap Nunó, 1 h 30
blurb: Pines, fishermen's huts and the clearest water on the west coast. The road is barriered in summer; in winter you can drive to the beach again.
tip: Saladeta is the second cove, over the rocks to the right.

name: Benirràs
walk: Benirràs → Cap Bernat viewpoint → Port de Sant Miquel ridge, 1 h 30
blurb: The north's sunset beach, with the finger rock of Cap Bernat in the frame. Sunday drums carry on in a smaller way through the autumn; the rest of the week it's yours.
tip: Exposed to the tramuntana — on a north-wind day go south instead.

name: Cala Xarraca & Xuclar
walk: Portinatx → Moscarter lighthouse coast path, 1 h each way
blurb: A deep bay with water like glass, rocks to swim off and the clay cliffs people still smear on their skin. Xuclar, next door, is the pebble cove with the boats.
tip: Best on a still morning — the bay faces north-east.

name: Aigües Blanques
walk: Aigües Blanques → Es Figueral cliffs → Pou des Lleó, 1 h 15
blurb: The sunrise beach: a long strip of pale sand under white cliffs, nudist by tradition, with the whole east coast stretching north. Dramatic when the sea is up.
tip: Steep steps down; the north end is the quiet one.

name: Cala Llenya
walk: Cala Llenya → Cala Nova → Es Canar, 50 min
blurb: A wide, flat, family beach between two pine headlands, with the shallowest, calmest water on the east coast. Quiet enough in winter to hear the pines.
tip: Parking fills early if Las Dalias is on.

name: Cala Boix
walk: Cala Boix → Cap Roig → Pou des Lleó, 40 min
blurb: Dark sand, red cliffs, Tagomago offshore and a bar on top of the steps that has been feeding fishermen for fifty years. The most 'winter' beach on the island.
tip: The restaurant on the cliff is the reason to come.

name: Cala Jondal
open: Yemanjá — open every day of the year. Tropicana: to confirm
walk: Cala Jondal → Es Xarco → Porroig coast path, 1 h
blurb: Pebbles, flat water and the big summer beach clubs, most of them shuttered from November. What's left is a long sheltered bay that's lovely on a bright winter day.
tip: Es Xarco, the next cove east, is the local one.

name: Platja d'en Bossa (north end)
open: Nassau Beach Club and Zazú — Thu–Sun; Casa del Mar Bonafé — to confirm days
walk: Bossa → Torre de sa Sal Rossa → Es Cavallet along the shore, 1 h
blurb: Three kilometres of sand that the island forgets in winter. The north end by the tower is the pretty bit: dunes, the old salt tower, and a walk all the way to Es Cavallet.
tip: Start at the Sa Sal Rossa tower car park, not the hotels.

name: Sa Caleta
open: Restaurante Sa Caleta — open in winter (days to confirm)
walk: Sa Caleta → the Phoenician settlement on the headland → Es Bol Nou red cliffs, 45 min
blurb: Red cliffs, a small beach of fishing huts, and the one restaurant on it, famous for its bullit de peix and the coffee with a caleta shot after. The Phoenician ruins on the point are the oldest settlement on the island.
tip: Order the bullit the day before; it's for two or more.

name: Cala Vadella
open: Cana Sofía — open in winter (days to confirm)
walk: Cala Vadella → Cala Carbó → Cala d'Hort coast path, 1 h 30
blurb: A deep, narrow inlet so sheltered the water is flat when the whole west coast is white. A village around it that half-empties in winter, and one restaurant on the seafront that stays.
tip: Walk round to Cala Carbó for the quieter cove.
